profile.name: Pritam
profile.shortBio: I write firmware and train models, and I care most about the overlap between the two. My work spans interrupt-driven C/C++ on microcontrollers, FPGA fault logic, ROS 2 autonomy stacks, and running ML inference on hardware that wasn't built for it.

about.fullBio:
I work at the boundary of embedded systems and machine learning. On the hardware side: C/C++ firmware, ESP-IDF, FPGA design, interrupt scheduling, UART/MQTT pipelines, and multi-node system architecture. On the ML side: Transformers, Diffusers, HuggingFace, PyTorch, contrastive retrieval, and diffusion models.

What connects both is the constraint problem. Getting a CubeSat watchdog to guarantee hard reboot in 1.5s, or fitting a VLM, a CLIP retrieval index, and a diffusion model inside 4 GB of VRAM — the interesting work is always about doing more with less.

My interests land in autonomous systems, edge AI, robotics perception, and anything that requires hardware and algorithms to meet halfway. I don't draw a hard line between firmware and ML; most of the problems worth solving sit somewhere in between.

experience.title: Embedded Application Developer (Intern)
description: Co-built Circuit Spell (spell.pcbcupid.com) from ideation: an AI agent that converts natural language into full PCB designs using 50+ proprietary Glyph modules, generating schematics, routed layouts, and 3D views exportable in Gerber/KiCad/PDF.
Prototyped core EDA subsystems: constraint-based component placement and auto-routing, de-risking the architecture before the production build.
Engineered multi-sensor IoT firmware in C/C++ on Glyph boards (C2, C6, H2) with interrupt-driven scheduling for high-precision industrial control tasks.

experience.title: Robotics Engineering Team Member & Mentor
description: Architected and built autonomous line-following robots using Arduino, achieving 95% path accuracy on complex competition tracks.
Led and mentored 15+ junior developers on embedded systems, PID control, and algorithm design.
